# Agents and Harnesses

- **An agent** is the autonomous actor — the thing that reasons, plans, uses tools, remembers, and pursues goals over multiple steps.
- **A harness** is the runtime / scaffolding that turns a raw language model into a working agent.
  - _**The harness** is the engine and chassis. **The agent** is the driver + the behavior that emerges once the model is running inside that chassis._


## Agent Harness Diagram
![Agent Harness Diagram](/assets/images/agent-harness-diagram.png "Agent Harness Diagram")



### More precise breakdown

| Concept | What it is | Examples |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Model** | The raw intelligence (weights) | Qwen, DeepSeek, Claude, Llama, Ajax (abliterated), etc. |
| **Harness** | The runtime that gives the model a loop, tools, memory, sandboxes, skills, messaging, persistence, etc. | Hermes, OpenClaw, goose, OpenHands, OpenCode, Agent Zero |
| **Agent** | The resulting autonomous system that actually does work | Copilot, OpenCode, Agent Zero |

**The harness determines:**
- How long the agent can run
- Whether it has persistent memory and can create its own skills
- What tools (MCP servers) it can reach
- Whether it lives in messaging apps, a terminal, a web UI, or a full Linux desktop
- How isolated / sandboxed its actions are
- How easy it is to observe, interrupt, or improve it

A good harness {Hermes, OPenCode, Agent Zero, OpenClaw, goose, etc.} dramatically changes what kind of agent you can actually have. A weak or missing harness leaves you with just a chatbot that forgets everything between messages

A harness is the runtime that gives a model a loop, tools, memory, and an
environment in which to act. It determines how long an agent can run, what it
can access, and how its work can be observed and controlled.

## Agentic development environments

An [{{< glossary "(ADE) Agentic Development Environment" popup="hover" >}}](https://davidgeeraerts.github.io/AI/appendices/glossary.html#ade-agentic-development-environment) is the editor, IDE, or terminal where a developer works with a coding agent. The harness is built around a repository: the agent reads the project, calls tools, and proposes changes, and the developer reviews them in place. OpenCode, OpenHands, Codex, Claude Code, Cline, and Aider are the coding harnesses this book already tracks. Cursor, Devin Desktop, Zed, and Kiro are the other environments in wide use that fit the same slot.

Cells were checked against each project's repository or docs in November 2026. The license column names the client or library.

| Tool | Type | License | Local models | Multi-agent | Strength |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [**OpenCode**](https://opencode.ai/) | Terminal, desktop, IDE | MIT | Ollama, LM Studio, and vLLM | Primary agents plus subagents (`build`, `plan`, `general`, `explore`) | Model-agnostic coding agent across terminal and editor |
| [**OpenHands**](https://openhands.dev/) | Local control center | MIT | Any LLM you configure. The app runs on your machine by default | Its own agent plus other agents over ACP, across local, remote, and cloud backends | Self-hosted canvas for several coding agents |
| [**Codex**](https://github.com/openai/codex) | CLI, IDE, cloud | Apache-2.0 (CLI source) | CLI: Ollama or LM Studio via `--oss`, or another Responses API server | Subagents, enabled by default in the CLI | Open terminal agent; the IDE extension shares its config |
| [**Claude Code**](https://code.claude.com/) | CLI and IDE | Proprietary (Anthropic terms) | Claude models. Routing to non-Claude models is unsupported | Subagents, background sessions, and agent teams | Anthropic's coding harness: permissions, hooks, and skills |

| [**Aider**](https://aider.chat/) | Terminal | Apache-2.0 | Local models, including Ollama | Single agent | Pair programming in the terminal |

[Roo Code](https://github.com/RooCodeInc/Roo-Code)'s README says the extension shut down on 15 May 2026 and names [Zoo Code](https://github.com/Zoo-Code-Org/Zoo-Code) (Apache-2.0, a community fork) and Cline as the places to go next.

## Agent orchestration

[{{< glossary "Agent orchestration" popup="hover" >}}](https://davidgeeraerts.github.io/AI/appendices/glossary.html#agent-orchestration) is the layer that coordinates more than one agent on one task. A [multi-agent system](https://davidgeeraerts.github.io/AI/appendices/glossary.html#multi-agent-system) is the architecture. The orchestrator assigns work, passes state, and decides whether agents run in parallel, in sequence, or under a supervisor. A [sub-agent](https://davidgeeraerts.github.io/AI/appendices/glossary.html#sub-agent) is the narrow worker that pattern usually spawns.

Libraries such as LangGraph, CrewAI, AG2, the OpenAI Agents SDK, and the Claude Agent SDK are how you build that coordination yourself. [SpyNEL](https://github.com/agent0ai/spynel), [Kortix](https://kortix.com/), and [Eigent](https://github.com/eigent-ai/eigent) are the coordinators this book already names: SpyNEL drives harnesses you already run, Kortix runs company work from a git repo, and Eigent is a desktop workforce.

The same November 2026 check applies here. Microsoft's [AutoGen](https://github.com/microsoft/autogen) repository is archived. Its code license is MIT (`LICENSE-CODE`) and its docs are CC-BY-4.0. The archived README sends new users to Microsoft Agent Framework. The upstream `microsoft/agent-framework` repository did not resolve when this table was written, so the row for that lineage is [AG2](https://github.com/ag2ai/ag2), the active project that still carries the AutoGen name.

| Tool | Type | License | Local models | Multi-agent | Strength |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [**LangGraph**](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/) | Library (Python and JavaScript) | MIT | None bundled. You supply the model client | Agents are nodes in a stateful graph. Deep Agents, built on LangGraph, adds subagents | Durable execution, checkpoints, and human interrupts |
| [**CrewAI**](https://docs.crewai.com/) | Library (Python) | MIT | Ollama and other providers through LiteLLM | Role-based crews, and Flows for event-driven branching | A short path from roles to a crew |
| [**AG2**](https://github.com/ag2ai/ag2) (formerly AutoGen) | Library (Python) | Apache-2.0 | `OllamaConfig`, or any OpenAI-compatible server (vLLM, LM Studio) | Agents cooperate through a hub and typed channels | Maintained line of the AutoGen idea |
| [**OpenAI Agents SDK**](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python) | Library (Python and JavaScript) | MIT | OpenAI APIs, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint | Handoffs and agents used as tools | Small surface: agents, guardrails, sessions, tracing |
| [**Claude Agent SDK**](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview) | Library (Python and TypeScript) | Anthropic Commercial Terms (Python package is MIT) | Claude models, same constraint as Claude Code | Subagents, hooks, and skills from Claude Code | Claude Code's loop as a library you run |
| [**SpyNEL**](https://github.com/agent0ai/spynel) | Orchestrator | MIT | No model of its own. Model support is the harness you attach | One chat drives many Codex, Claude Code, and other harness sessions | Reuses existing coding harnesses; task state stays in Markdown |
| [**Kortix CompanyOS**](https://github.com/kortix-ai/CompanyOS) | Company harness | Elastic License 2.0 | Any model, in Kortix's cloud or yours | A fleet of agents for ongoing company work | Skills, memory, and connectors in one git repo |
| [**Eigent**](https://github.com/eigent-ai/eigent) | Desktop | Apache-2.0 | Local deployment; any model you choose | A parallel workforce, or one meta agent | Desktop multi-agent workforce built on CAMEL |

LangGraph does not pick a model or an agent shape. CrewAI's Ollama path is documented as a LiteLLM provider. The Claude Agent SDK overview says use of the SDK is governed by Anthropic's Commercial Terms, including when a component's own file says MIT.

## Supporting infrastructure

- **MCP (Model Context Protocol)** connects agents to tools and services.
- Sandboxed execution environments such as Docker, Daytona, Modal, E2B, and
  browser infrastructure help isolate agent actions.
- Persistent memory and agent-written skills support longer-running work.
- **SpyNEL** orchestrates existing coding harnesses. See [Agent orchestration](#agent-orchestration).
- **DOX / AGENTS.md** hierarchies give agents maintainable project context.




## [agents.md](https://agents.md/)


#### Evaluating AGENTS.md: Are Repository-Level Context Files Helpful for Coding Agents?
[Evaluating AGENTS.md: Are Repository-Level Context Files Helpful...](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.11988)

Repository context files can affect coding-agent performance [@gloaguen2026agentsmd].

| Condition | Effect on success rate | Effect on cost / steps |
|---|---|---|
| LLM-generated context files | Slightly worse on average (~ –0.5% on SWE-bench Lite, ~ –2% to –3% on the new bench; negative in most configs) | +20–23% inference cost; +2.5–4 extra steps per task |
| Human-written context files | Modest average gain (~ +4% on the developer-file benchmark) | Still + up to ~19% cost / more steps |
| Overall | “Does not generally improve task success rates” | Clear, consistent cost increase |


Practical takeaway that matches the evidence: Keep any AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md extremely short. Prefer only non-discoverable facts (exact test/build commands that differ from the obvious, hard “never touch X”, unusual tooling). Long files that restate what is already in the code, README, or package.json are the ones most likely to waste tokens for little or no gain.



## Enterprise-level agentic engineering

### [Kortix CompanyOS](https://kortix.com/)
> is a source-available, cloud-native agent harness (Elastic License 2.0) designed to run a company’s work as code.
> Kortix sits above personal coding or messaging agents. It is the operating system layer for teams that want agents doing real, ongoing company work (sales, support, engineering triage, marketing loops, ops, etc.) while keeping configuration, memory, and outcomes reviewable, versioned, and human-gated.

| Aspect | Kortix CompanyOS | Personal harnesses |
|---|---|---|
| Core idea | Company as code; agents + skills + memory in one git repo | Personal agent that lives with you (messaging, coding, memory) |
| Scale | Team / organization, swarms, event-driven | Individual or small-team |
| Governance | Change requests, permissions-as-code, agent principals | Lighter or tool-level permissions |
| State | Shared company memory + per-session computers | Per-user curated memory + skills |
| Best fit | Internal tooling, ops, multi-agent company workflows | Daily personal leverage, coding, always-on assistant |
